introduction: Tailored for SSC CGL Tier-2 (Mains) and technical IT Officer exams, this advanced module covers complex system initialization terms, programmable memory variations, and processor speed metrics.

core_concepts.title: Advanced Memory Variations
core_concepts.description:
- PROM: Programmable Read-Only Memory
- EPROM: Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory (Erased using UV light).
- EEPROM: Electrically Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory (Erased using electrical signals; used in modern flash drives).

core_concepts.title: System Initialization & Power
core_concepts.description:
- POST: Power-On Self-Test (The diagnostic testing sequence run by BIOS immediately after powering on).
- SMPS: Switched-Mode Power Supply (The main power supply unit inside a desktop cabinet).
- UPS: Uninterruptible Power Supply

core_concepts.title: User Interfaces
core_concepts.description:
- GUI: Graphical User Interface (Windows/Mouse based).
- CLI: Command Line Interface (Text/Keyboard based, like MS-DOS).

core_concepts.title: Processing Speed Metrics
core_concepts.description:
- MIPS: Million Instructions Per Second (Used to measure CPU speed).
- FLOPS: Floating-Point Operations Per Second (Used to measure Supercomputer speed).

important_entities.name: SMPS
important_entities.significance: Converts AC power from the wall socket to the lower voltages required by the internal components of a computer.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Mains exams will test the 'E's. The first 'E' is always Electrically, the second 'E' is Erasable. **Electrically Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory**. Do not mix up the order.
Options will include 'Switch-Mode Power Supply' or 'Switched-Machine Power Supply'. The correct technical term is **Switched-Mode Power Supply**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Whenever you see supercomputer speed in a question, look for FLOPS. Remember that 'Floating-Point' is hyphenated and represents complex decimal mathematics.

exam_strategy_tips: For Tier-2, GUI (Graphical User Interface) and POST (Power-On Self-Test) are absolute must-knows. Be extremely careful with the word 'Test' in POST; examiners often substitute it with 'System' or 'Terminal'.
